title: Classical upbringing and first jazz via his sister
summary: Raised on classics and opera; at eight his sister introduced him to jazz through Bunk Johnson. He also took painting and gave up piano for economic reasons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, what kind of music were you interested in when you were young?

Well, I heard nothing but classics until I was eight. And when I was eight, my sister introduced me to jazz. My sister was an opera singer, by the way. And she introduced me to jazz when I was about eight. Through Bunk Johnson. And my mother used to turn on the Metropolitan Opera ! But when she left the room, I'd switch over to a station that played Dixie in the afternoon. You know, the afternoon Metropolitan broadcast from New York. So that's how I became interested in jazz, basically. I was about eight then. Around that time, I was also taking painting. And I had been playing piano, but I had to give that up through economic reasons.
Did your father play around the house?
No, he didn't have time to. He was quite busy working generally. He was doing the war, you
know? Who did you listen to? Who did you remember? You said Bunk Johnson for long, or else?
